answer_text:
Let

\[
Y_i = X_i^2,\qquad X_i \sim U[0,1].
\]

Then \(Y_i\) are i.i.d. and

\[
\mathbb{E}[Y_i]=\mathbb{E}[X_i^2]=\int_0^1 x^2\,dx=\frac13.
\]

Also,

\[
\mathbb{E}[Y_i^2]=\mathbb{E}[X_i^4]=\int_0^1 x^4\,dx=\frac15,
\]

so

\[
\operatorname{Var}(Y_i)=\frac15-\left(\frac13\right)^2=\frac{4}{45}>0.
\]

Now

\[
\frac{D_n}{\sqrt n}
= \sqrt{\frac{X_1^2+\cdots+X_n^2}{n}}
= \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
F_{D_n/\sqrt n}\left(\frac1{\sqrt3}\right)
=
\mathbb{P}\left(\frac{D_n}{\sqrt n}\le \frac1{\sqrt3}\right)
=
\mathbb{P}\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i \le \frac13\right).
\]

By the Central Limit Theorem,

\[
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i - n/3}{\sqrt{n}\,\sqrt{4/45}}
\ \xrightarrow{d}\ N(0,1).
\]

Hence,

\[
\mathbb{P}\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i \le \frac13\right)
=
\mathbb{P}\left(
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i - n/3}{\sqrt{n}\,\sqrt{4/45}}
\le 0
\right)
\to \Phi(0)=\frac12.
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{\frac12}
\]
